Ghoendea is the sole professor who has helped me construct the fundamental mathematical logic that will stay with me from my undergraduate studies. He does not view mathematics and math education as mere exams directed towards students in certain courses; rather, he approaches his work with a desire to teach mathematical principles that will truly be remembered in the minds of his audience. In this sense, in my opinion, he is one of the rare individuals not only at Bilkent University but also in Turkey and even globally. Negative comments about him stem precisely from this reason. People worldwide, and unfortunately especially in Turkish culture, are accustomed to completing a task with maximum benefit without putting in too much effort, shifting the responsibility of their own work onto others, and incapable of critical thinking or delving deeply into a subject. Therefore, someone like Ghoendea, who has developed these skills and tries to instill them in his students, can easily become an object of hatred. As someone who constantly bears the "punishment" of thinking deeply about a subject in my own life, I can empathize with him. The general workaholism of students, their laziness, leading a life blindly following the breadcrumbs of existence like an insect, makes life even more challenging for people like me and Ghoendea, unfortunately (speaking frankly, ego aside). If he happens to read this comment, I would like to convey to him my self-imposed motto: "You don't get mad at a barking dog, nor do you let yourself be emotionally affected by it." I thank him not only for his lessons on mathematics but also for the courses filled with concepts on how to approach any complex subject by breaking it down into simple steps and understanding it (some of which felt like a concert to me). The "price difference" between the concerns in this comment and the triviality of the complaints in negative reviews says a lot to me.

He was also ardent and keen on making our life easier especially by giving us enough time during the exams. I just wish he didn't rush the quizzes during the first weeks following Corona since they we were so burdened with everyone wanting to give his or hers assignments. In any case, Dr. Aurelian has changed my life for the good, thank you for that!
